_comment: Default monster-head registry for Civillis.
This file demonstrates how to register skull types and tune
their gameplay effects as head-based debuff items.
Modpack authors can add custom JSON files in
data/<namespace>/civil_heads/ to register/override head types.
skull_type: must match SkullBlock.SkullType.toString() for vanilla,
or a custom string for modded heads.
entity_type: target mob type used when this skull is selected for conversion
(may be null if this skull should only contribute head count).
enabled: master switch (default true). If false, this head type becomes
purely decorative to Civillis head mechanics.
convert: whether this head joins the conversion pool (default true).
convert=false still contributes count/debuff pressure, but this
skull type will never be chosen as the replacement mob.
dimensions: optional dimension whitelist (e.g. ["minecraft:the_nether"]).
If omitted: active everywhere. Else decorative outside the list.
Runtime behavior (with active Podium of Spawning / farm shrine):
eligible heads inside the shrine pocket become the debuff/control layer
for natural spawns (local bypass + distant attraction + optional conversion).
Heads outside an active pocket do nothing.
Conversion:
chance = min(100%, headCount x 10%) on each natural spawn
(1 converting head = 10%, 10+ = 100%).
If there are no converting heads, conversion does not run.
Converted mob type is picked from placed converting heads.
Loading order: files are loaded alphabetically per namespace.
Later entries with the same skull_type override earlier ones
(full replacement — re-specify all fields you need).
Tip: to disable a specific head type incrementally, override it
with 'enabled': false. Example for a modpack that wants zombie
heads to be purely decorative:
{ "skull_type": "ZOMBIE", "enabled": false }
Set 'replace': true to clear ALL previously loaded head types
(useful for modpacks that want a complete custom table).
--- Mod compatibility ---
If a mod adds new skull types via custom AbstractSkullBlock
subclasses (with custom SkullType enums), you can register
them here by adding entries with the matching skull_type string.
Example for a mod that adds a Blaze head with type 'BLAZE':
{ "skull_type": "BLAZE", "entity_type": "minecraft:blaze" }
Note: mods that use PLAYER heads with custom textures (such as
All The Heads, Just Mob Heads) are NOT supported — our system
sees them all as skull_type 'PLAYER' and cannot distinguish
which mob they represent. Only mods using distinct SkullType
values are automatically compatible.
